516a2ee955e1b623f0ba903a3e9749c1250d8b2f.summary: Year-end review by the Intezer security blog of Linux threats in 2020, not a single-incident report. It says APTs have long targeted Linux, mainly attributed to Russia, China and North Korea, and that a Linux version of WellMail was disclosed in July, attributed by the UK NCSC to APT29. Cybercrime groups also moved to Linux, including a Linux TrickBot sample and IPStorm, and existing tools such as Penquin (Turla) and QNAPCrypt were updated. Golang is highlighted for cross-platform malware that is hard for antivirus engines to detect, with a Carbanak Linux sample as an example. The post ends…

51672fafe669cf99d78fbf7393084e04cf008325.summary: Mandiant report on UNC3886, a suspected China-nexus espionage actor. It describes exploitation of zero-day flaws in VMware and Fortinet products to reach guest VMs, ESXi hypervisors and TACACS+ servers since late 2021. It covers the REPTILE and MEDUSA rootkits, MOPSLED and RIFLESPINE backdoors that use GitHub and Google Drive for C2, backdoored SSH binaries that harvest credentials, a TACACS+ credential-capture effort, and VMCI backdoors. Victims are mainly in North America, Southeast Asia and Oceania, in government, telecom, technology, aerospace, defense and energy sectors.

hedges: Mandiant describes UNC3886 as a suspected China-nexus cyber espionage actor.
The FortiOS-exploiting threat actor is only suspected to be UNC3886.
Mandiant assessed the use of MEDUSA to be experimental alternatives of REPTILE and SSH keyloggers.
The objectives of the threat actor were initially unclear due to limited visibility and the extensive use of rootkits, tools, and scripts.
It is reasonable to assume that the threat actor abandoned the idea of using MOPSLED.LINUX and RIFLESPINE as backdoors.
REPTILE appeared to be the first option to establish a foothold and possibly the last resort for maintaining access due to its small footprints.
Early development is potentially indicating the actor has been developing and/or operating this rootkit for some time.
